html:
I was revisiting Beyond today and happened to see your question.

I also started listening to Beyond, the Hong Kong rock band, in ninth grade, and I’ve kept at it ever since: 16 years now.

The first song I heard was “Silent Years,” which a classmate played. I’d hardly listened to any Cantonese songs before and thought, what on earth is this? Then somehow I came across “Really Love You” and was instantly hooked. I borrowed that classmate’s VCD (yes, you heard right, a VCD, the kind you put in a disc player) and never gave it back… When he asked, I said I’d lost it…

On it was Beyond’s most classic concert, Live 1991. How hooked was I? I treated my afternoon nap as sacred, yet every so often I’d skip it to play the VCD all the way through, and then be dead tired all afternoon. Teachers didn’t let us listen to music at school, so that was the only way.

Because of Beyond, I bought a guitar right after the college entrance exam, and I’ve played on and off ever since. My biggest dream is to go out on the street and belt out Beyond songs at the top of my voice. Sounds like a line from The Voice of China…

Luckily my teachers were nothing like yours. In high school I sang Beyond’s “No More Hesitation” in class a few times, and it felt amazing.

There are plenty of good songs, singers and bands out there. But what makes you truly love Beyond, besides the sighs over the legendary life of Wong Ka Kui, the frontman who died at 31, is the band’s attitude toward music, and toward life and living. After all the empty love songs, Beyond is a real eye-opener, like suddenly seeing hope in life itself.

Every song gets old eventually, even Beyond’s. But the magic of Beyond is that every so often you dig their songs out again, play them obsessively, and get fired up all over again.

Later I also came to like Jay Chou and other heartthrob pop stars, but Beyond’s place has never been taken. That same kind of madness didn’t come back until this year, when I watched Bohemian Rhapsody and fell hard for Queen, as feverishly as I did back then. I listened to all their songs and watched the documentaries, the behind-the-scenes stories and so on. Beyond and Queen turn out to have so much in common: original rock bands, diverse and muscular musical styles, lead singers who died young… If there’s a difference, it’s that Beyond gives you youthful anger and reflection, while Queen gives you strength.


Music, like writing, never goes out of date. Like Ka Kui and Freddie, it endures, and its spirit lives on.
